clue.text: Bird put up with stifling warmth

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so one piece is wrapped inside the other

parts.note: to wear something is to tolerate it
heat is warmth

explanation.surface: Someone endures a bird despite the oppressive heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up with' reads like a link phrase, but it supplies the outer word, and 'stifling' smothers the warmth inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small migratory songbird of open country.

clue.text: Unsolicited -e-mails, we deduce from charts, rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: maps are charts

explanation.surface: Someone works out from graphs that junk mail is on the increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns MAPS upwards in this down clue; 'we deduce from' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk messages sent in bulk to inboxes are known by this name.

clue.text: Mild end of spring in country

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the country's name

parts.note: Benin is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word spring

explanation.surface: Spring's close brings mild weather in some land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes G from 'spring', and 'in' puts it inside BENIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign weather or a benign manner is gentle and harmless.

clue.text: Rules, being erratic, I changed

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits altering the rules because they were unpredictable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges ERRATIC plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are the standards or tests by which things are judged.

clue.text: Account, in detail, salesman's written up, identifying substance used in candles

indicators.note: in places the account abbreviation within the other letters
in a down clue, written up means the letters are set down bottom to top

parts.note: an item is a detail or particular
a rep is a salesman, and the 's makes it plural-looking REPS

explanation.surface: A salesman's itemised account is written up, naming the waxy stuff in candles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' turns detail and salesman's together, bottom to top in this down clue, and only then does 'in' slot the account letters in, so they stay forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Spermaceti is the waxy matter from the sperm whale's head, once used to make fine candles.

clue.text: Time consumed by anxiety over large alliance

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above the next
consumed by means one piece is swallowed up inside the other

parts.note: care is worry or anxiety
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Worry eats up time over some big partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed by' puts T inside CARE, and 'over' sets that above L in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is an association of firms that combine to control prices.

clue.text: Man in field, mostly, by day?

definitions.text: Man in field, mostly, by day?

parts.words: Man in field, mostly, by day?
parts.note: a man out in a field with a flock; the question mark nods to the carol whose flock-watchers worked by night

explanation.surface: Someone asks who is out in the field, chiefly during daylight.
explanation.walkthrough: The carol 'While shepherds watched their flocks by night' sets the night scene; the clue says this man is usually out there by day.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who tends sheep spends most of his working day in the fields.

clue.text: Splendid guess

explanation.definitionFit: Divine is informal for wonderful, and to divine is to guess by intuition.

clue.text: Crude wrapping is put round power tool

indicators.note: wrapping means the first piece encloses what follows

parts.note: raw means crude or unrefined

indicators.note: put round means the little word surrounds the power letter

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A crude covering is fitted around an electric tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power tool' reads as one phrase, but 'power' gives only its letter; 'put round' and 'wrapping' nest the pieces two deep.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripsaw is a coarse saw for cutting wood along the grain.

clue.text: Conceal prize

explanation.definitionFit: To palm something is to hide it in the hand, and the palm is a leaf awarded as a symbol of victory.

clue.text: Furious about disruption of event that's long established

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: irate means furious

indicators.note: disruption of says the letters of the next word are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone is angry that a long-running event has been disrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disruption of' scrambles the five letters of 'event', and 'about' sets the anger word around that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: An inveterate habit is deep-rooted, having lasted a long time.

clue.text: Grey animal's abode is at end of meadow

indicators.note: is at end of puts the animal's home after the meadow word

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow
a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: A grey creature's home lies at the far end of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: Lea is a poetic or dialect word for a meadow, common in crosswords; 'is at end of' sets the den after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden skies are dull and grey like the metal lead.

clue.text: Crush formed by number after attention, following beautiful person

indicators.note: following means the attention word comes after the beautiful person
after means the number comes after the attention word

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
an ear is attention, as in 'lend an ear'
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A romantic crush builds up after a stunner catches someone's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crush' looks like a noun for an infatuation, but it is the verb, to dispirit; 'following' and 'after' fix the order of the three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush someone's spirits is to dismay or discourage them.

clue.text: As a rule drama's supplied by medium in gathering

parts.note: No (or Noh) is classical Japanese drama

indicators.note: in puts the size letter inside the gathering word

parts.note: a rally is a mass gathering

explanation.surface: Theatre is usually provided by a psychic at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' looks like a spiritualist at a seance; it is only the clothing size letter, which 'in' puts inside the gathering word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done normally happens usually, as a matter of routine.

clue.text: On receiving inspiration after retirement start again

indicators.note: receiving means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: retirement suggests withdrawing backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a muse is a source of inspiration

explanation.surface: After retiring, someone finds new inspiration and takes up work again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' reads as stopping work, but here it means going backwards; 'receiving' then puts the reversed source of inspiration inside the 'on' word.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to begin again after a pause.

clue.text: Calm German with crowd going around island

indicators.note: going around means the two pieces enclose the island letter

parts.note: mit is the German word for with
the gate is the crowd attending a sports match

explanation.surface: Someone soothes a German as a mob surrounds an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' tempts a solver to write G; the two words 'German with' together give the German for 'with'. The crowd is a sports gate, and 'going around' encloses the island letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To mitigate is to ease or lessen the severity of something.

clue.text: Clear head? Fool doesn't have one

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

indicators.note: doesn't have means a letter is taken away from the fool word

parts.note: a nit is a fool
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A clear-headed person asks whether an idiot lacks one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear head?' looks like one phrase; the definition is 'Clear' alone, and 'doesn't have one' strips the Roman one from the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent means obvious or plainly evident.

clue.text: Plant to notice, fine and soft

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
lax means slack or soft

explanation.surface: A list of qualities for a plant: noticeable, fine and soft.
explanation.walkthrough: Four pieces in a row: TO, AD, F, LAX.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadflax is a wild flower with yellow snapdragon-like blooms.

clue.text: Composer with wide, varied range

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

indicators.note: varied means the letters of the next word are mixed up

explanation.surface: A composer has a broad and varied musical range.
explanation.walkthrough: W for wide is a cricket scoring abbreviation; 'varied' mixes up 'range'.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Wagner was the German composer of the Ring cycle operas.

clue.text: Number sitting inside welcomed, for the most part, a drink

indicators.note: sitting inside places the number letter within the shortened word
for the most part means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: greeted means welcomed

explanation.surface: A guest is mostly made welcome and offered a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops the last letter of the welcome word, and 'sitting inside' tucks the number letter into what is left, before the final 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is unfermented tea, a popular drink in East Asia.

clue.text: Armies with king moving forward to arrive at port

indicators.note: moving forward means the king's letter shifts to the front of the word

parts.note: hordes are great armies or crowds
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: Armies led by a king advance to reach a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving forward' takes the R of HORDES to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek island city and harbour.

clue.text: Tons, not completely scurrilous, relating to a group

indicators.note: not completely means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: ribald means coarse or scurrilous

explanation.surface: Weighty but crude stuff concerning a community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tons' gives only its abbreviation; 'not completely' trims the last letter from the word for coarse or scurrilous.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal describes things belonging to a tribe, a social group.

clue.text: Poorly made craft overturned before start

indicators.note: before puts the reversed piece ahead of the next
overturned means the craft word is turned upside down, read backwards in a down clue

parts.note: art is craft or skill
to shy is to start or jump in alarm, as a horse does

explanation.surface: A shoddily built boat capsized before setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like a boat that has capsized; it is skill, turned over by 'overturned', and 'start' is the verb for jumping in alarm, as a horse shies.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashy goods are cheap and of poor quality.

clue.text: Facts about bullfight? On the contrary, errors

indicators.note: about signals that one piece goes around another
on the contrary reverses the stated roles, so the bullfight goes around the facts

parts.note: corrida is Spanish for bullfight
gen is slang for facts or information

explanation.surface: Someone asks about facts on a bullfight, then calls them mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, the facts would go round the bullfight; 'On the contrary' swaps the roles so the bullfight encloses the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrigenda are a list of mistakes to be corrected in a printed book.

clue.text: What litigant has to lose is plain — there's little argument

indicators.note: has to lose means the named word is taken away from the litigant word

parts.note: a plaintiff is a litigant who brings a case
taken as written

explanation.surface: A court party clearly stands to lose, so there's no real dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to lose' takes PLAIN from PLAINTIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty quarrel.

clue.text: Instrument playing part in impromptu band

indicators.note: playing part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instrument joins in with a band that is jamming on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing part in' finds the instrument across 'impromptU BAnd'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is a large low-pitched brass instrument.

clue.text: Hate, in fact, set editor back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone loathes it when a fact puts the editor back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the run TSETED in 'facT SET EDitor', and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe intensely.

clue.text: Wine bottle tramp found amid quantity of paper

indicators.note: found amid means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets
a hobo is a tramp

explanation.surface: A vagrant's wine bottle turns up in a stack of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: A rehoboam is one of the big champagne bottle sizes named after biblical kings; a ream is 500 sheets of paper, and 'found amid' puts the tramp inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehoboam is a large champagne bottle holding six standard bottles.
